verdict.rationale: Agents connect over MCP with OAuth 2.1 instead of API keys, which is a first-party credential mechanism for agents (docs-7). Access can be scoped with roles down to the table and column (docs-24), and agents run on isolated, read-only compute (docs-12), so least-privilege agent access is plausible. No evidence explicitly shows issuing a scoped, agent-specific credential or token with chosen permissions, or that OAuth grants can be bound to restricted roles. Missing for 10: documented issuance of per-agent scoped tokens/credentials, explicit linkage of OAuth/MCP grants to role scopes, revocation/expiry controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.
